model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, factors that determine the survival of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) with lung metastasis alone include age, disease-free interval (DFI), and treatment modality. Combined modality treatment appears to benefit patients with DFI > 1 year, but not those with DFI ≤ 1 year. Patients treated with combined therapy had significantly longer median overall survival (73.7 months vs. 46.2 months) and post-metastasis survival (45.6 months vs. 23.7 months) compared to those treated with chemotherapy alone. This suggests that combined modality treatment may be indicated for selected cases in this population.
long_answer: Age ≤ 45 years, DFI>1 year, and the combined therapy were good prognostic factors for NPC patients with lung metastasis(es) alone. The combination of local therapy and the basic chemotherapy should be considered for these patients with DFI>1 year.

model_explanation: Yes, minimally invasive mitral valve repair with artificial chords is considered reproducible and applicable in routine surgery. The study of 426 consecutive patients found that all patients remained without or with trace mitral regurgitation after follow-up ranging from 3-60 months. No neochord de-insertion or rupture occurred, and no reoperations were required. This suggests that artificial chords are a reliable alternative to traditional techniques in minimally invasive mitral valve repair.
long_answer: Minimally invasive mitral valve repair using neochords provided a high rate of repair, reproducible results in a routine cardiac surgery setting and stable repair during follow-up. This has become our preferred technique for mitral valve surgery.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, receipt of hospice care in nursing homes improves the management of pain at the end of life. The study found that 51% of hospice residents received regular treatment for daily pain, compared to 33% of non-hospice residents. This difference remained significant even after controlling for clinical confounders, suggesting that hospice care was associated with better pain management. Overall, the data suggest that hospice care is linked to more effective analgesic use and improved pain management in nursing home residents at the end of life.
long_answer: Findings suggest that analgesic management of daily pain is better for nursing home residents enrolled in hospice than for those not enrolled in hospice.The prescribing practices portrayed by this study reveal that many dying nursing home residents in daily pain are receiving no analgesic treatment or are receiving analgesic treatment inconsistent with AMDA and other pain management guidelines. Improving the analgesic management of pain in nursing homes is essential if high-quality end-of-life care in nursing homes is to be achieved.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, intensive chemotherapy appears to be safe for rural cancer patients. The Townsville Cancer Centre's teleoncology model has been shown to be effective in providing equality of care to rural patients with similar outcomes to urban patients. A retrospective audit found no significant differences in dose intensities or toxicity rates between urban and rural patients receiving chemotherapy for metastatic colorectal and node-positive breast cancers. Additionally, a study on non-small cell lung carcinoma found that cytostatic treatment was associated with improved survival, indicating the safety of intensive chemotherapy in rural cancer patients.
long_answer: It appears safe to administer intensive chemotherapy regimens at standard doses to rural patients without increased morbidity or mortality. Support for general practitioners through phone or videoconferencing may reduce the safety concerns.

model_explanation: Yes, the urinary biomarker assessment is considered a non-invasive approach to assessing tubulointerstitial lesions of the solitary kidney. The study found significant correlations between urinary biomarkers (NAG, alpha-1-microglobulin, albuminuria) and eGFR in both acquired and congenital solitary kidneys, indicating their potential utility as biomarkers for monitoring kidney function. Although the study was cross-sectional, it suggests that urinary biomarker assessment may be a useful non-invasive method for evaluating tubulointerstitial lesions in solitary kidneys, potentially enabling early detection and monitoring of kidney disease progression.
long_answer: Urinary biomarkers allow a non-invasive, sensitive, early assessment of the tubular lesions of the SK. Urinary biomarkers of PT injury parallel renal function decline, thus complementing the estimation of GFR. Monitoring of PT dysfunction is mandatory in patients with SK.

model_explanation: The evidence suggests that open access endoscopy may not provide patients with adequate information and preparation for the procedure. Patients referred for open access endoscopy reported receiving significantly less information about their procedure compared to those from specialized clinics (Evidence 1). This may lead to decreased patient satisfaction, particularly with procedures performed without sedation. On the other hand, patients from GI subspecialty clinics who underwent procedures under conscious sedation had higher satisfaction scores and felt better at follow-up. This highlights the importance of adequate patient preparation and information in open access endoscopy.
long_answer: Patients undergoing open access procedures are less likely to be properly informed about their endoscopic procedure. Our results indicate that with open access endoscopy, a defined mechanism needs to be in place for communication of endoscopic results to the patient.

model_explanation: Yes, viral infections appear to play a role in benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). A retrospective study found that serologic analysis of viral agents showed higher values in the BPPV group compared to the control group for most viruses. Seasonal variation was also observed, with increased viral infection rates during specific months (e.g., March-May and September). However, it is essential to note that these findings do not establish a causal relationship between viral infections and BPPV. Further studies are needed to understand the mechanisms underlying this association.
long_answer: BPPV is associated with positive viral serology, particularly during certain months of the year, mainly in spring and autumn. Viral infection might promote BPPV attacks due to the development of vestibulopathy or induce secondary BPPV via viral infection-related neurolabyrinthitis.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, it appears that reducing spasticity does not necessarily translate into functional benefit for stroke patients. While there is a significant negative correlation between maximum changes in spasticity and arm function (rho = -0.2822), indicating a relationship between reduction in spasticity and improvement in function, this relationship is not always linear or causal. In some cases, the improvement in spasticity occurs before the improvement in function, while in others, it happens concurrently. This suggests that reducing spasticity may be a necessary but not sufficient condition for functional benefit to occur.
long_answer: Using a targeted meta-analytic approach, it is possible to demonstrate that reducing spasticity in the arm is associated with a significant improvement in arm function.

model_explanation: The retromandibular transparotid approach is considered a reliable option for the surgical treatment of condylar fractures. According to Evidence 1, retrospective evaluation of 25 patients showed that this approach was safe and reliable, with most patients experiencing restored preinjury occlusion and temporomandibular joint health, and satisfactory esthetic outcomes. There were no permanent neurologic impairments or major postoperative complications observed. The study suggests that the retromandibular transparotid approach is a viable alternative to other surgical approaches for condylar fracture treatment, providing good functional and aesthetic outcomes.
long_answer: According to the results of the present study, the retromandibular transparotid approach is a viable and safe approach for the surgical treatment of condylar fractures.

model_explanation: According to the retrieved evidence, ventricular arrhythmias in athletes can subside over time. A follow-up study of 192 athletes with ventricular arrhythmias during an exercise test found that those who had ventricular premature beats (VPB) and/or ventricular couplets and/or non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) during their initial test had far fewer arrhythmias in the follow-up test. Additionally, a study on exercise training effects found that trained individuals showed reduced ventricular repolarization duration and QT/RR slope, suggesting potential benefits of physical activity in reducing ventricular arrhythmias over time.
long_answer: Athletes engaged in competitive sports are more likely to develop ventricular arrhythmias during exercise. These arrhythmias subside over time when athletes are engaged in non-competitive sports.

model_explanation: Yes, complex coronary lesions are more frequent in patients with diabetes mellitus. A study of 1,014 consecutive patients found that patients with diabetes had a significantly higher prevalence of bifurcation and ostial lesions compared to nondiabetics (9.8% vs. 4.3% for bifurcation lesions, 38.4% vs. 29.2% for ostial lesions). Multivariate analysis also identified diabetes and age as independent predictors for these complex lesions. This suggests that patients with diabetes mellitus are at a higher risk of developing more severe and complex coronary artery disease.
long_answer: Complex coronary lesions such as bifurcation and ostial lesions were significantly more common in diabetic patients than in nondiabetic patients. Greater age and the presence of DM were independent predictors for these complex lesions. These results may help to explain the poor prognosis of coronary artery disease among diabetic patients.

model_explanation: According to the provided evidence, yes, dogs can potentially prime autistic children for therapy. A study found that exposure to a therapy dog increased positive behaviors and reduced negative behaviors in an autistic child during structured activities with a therapist. This suggests that the presence of a dog may have a priming effect, making the child more receptive to the therapeutic interaction. While the exact mechanisms are unclear, this finding supports the potential benefits of canine-assisted therapy for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
long_answer: These findings are in accordance with previous experimental work and provide additional support for the assertion that dogs can prime autistic children for therapy. Ultimately, this study may contribute toward a change for full acceptance of canine-assisted therapy programs within the medical milieu. Additional studies using a similar research protocol on more autistic children will certainly help professionals to work on the most effective methods to individually serve this population through canine-assisted interventions.

model_explanation: According to the retrieved evidence, there is an association between socioeconomic status and quality of life in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients. A study found that 57% of patients with lower socioeconomic status had more health problems, less functioning, and more symptoms compared to affluent patients (Evidence 1). Another study revealed that a patient's self-reported health-related quality of life was a significant independent prognostic factor for survival in non-small cell lung cancer patients, suggesting potential social determinants of health influence outcomes. However, the impact of socioeconomic status on quality of life may vary over time.
long_answer: At baseline assessment patients of lower socioeconomic status showed lower health related quality of life. Since there was no clear trend at follow-up assessment this suggests that patients from different socioeconomic status responded to treatment similarly. In general, the findings suggest that quality of life is not only the outcome of the disease and its treatment, but is also highly dependent on each patients' socioeconomic characteristics.

model_explanation: Yes, there is a training model for retroperitoneoscopy. A study using piglets developed a standard retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy (RPN) training model to establish an experimental learning curve. The model included performing RPNs with three ports and recording intraoperative data. The study found that an experimental learning curve of eight cases was sufficient, and the findings suggest that RPN can simulate the whole procedure from creating space to nephrectomy completion. This model provides a framework for teaching and practicing retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy, particularly in laparoscopy training programs.
long_answer: RPN in a porcine model is feasible and could be very useful for teaching and practicing retroperitoneoscopy.

model_explanation: Yes, the type of remission is an important risk factor for relapse. A study found that patients who achieved partial remission had a higher rate of relapse (91.4%) compared to those in complete remission (51.3%). Partial remission was identified as the most powerful predictive factor for relapse. This suggests that achieving full recovery from depression may not be sufficient, and even partial improvement can increase the risk of relapse. Therefore, it is essential to consider the type of remission when developing treatment plans to minimize the risk of relapse in patients with major depressive episode.
long_answer: At medium term, relapse rates for a major depressive episode are high. Partial remission after a depressive episode seems to be an important predictive factor for relapses in a 4-year follow-up.

model_explanation: The implementation of epidural analgesia for labor has shown significant progress, with epidural use increasing from 15.5% to 51% over the 2-year audit period. Patient satisfaction levels were good, and effectiveness was reported. However, there is a concern that not all women receive epidural analgesia, especially in settings where it may be perceived as an additional treatment or resource-intensive option. The retrieved evidence does not provide specific information on the standardization of effective analgesia for all women, but overall suggests that epidural analgesia can significantly improve pain management during childbirth.
long_answer: Present audit shows that the process of implementation of labor analgesia was quick, successful and safe, notwithstanding the identification of one cluster of women with suboptimal response to epidural analgesia that need to be further studies, overall pregnant womens'adhesion to labor analgesia was satisfactory.

model_explanation: No, the Barthel Index alone is not considered an adequate measure of longer-term quality of life and outcome in stroke patients. The Barthel Index primarily measures activities of daily living (ADL) and does not account for other important aspects of quality of life, such as emotional well-being, social interaction, or physical mobility. Studies have shown correlations between the Barthel Index and other outcome measures like the SF36, Nottingham Health Profile, and Life Satisfaction Index, suggesting that a comprehensive assessment is needed to accurately evaluate stroke outcomes.
long_answer: The place of the Barthel index as the standard outcome measure for populations of stroke patients is still justified for long term follow up, and may be a proxy for different outcome measures intended for the assessment of other domains.

model_explanation:
A special interest in laparoscopy is not indicated to significantly impact the treatment of acute cholecystitis. In Study 1, the outcomes for patients treated by laparoscopic specialists (LS group) and general surgeons who perform only laparoscopic cholecystectomy (GS group) showed similar rates of successful surgery, complications, and hospital length of stay. The LS group had a shorter median postoperative hospital stay, but this was not found to be a significant factor in logistic regression analysis.

Study 2 suggests that male sex may affect outcomes, such as conversion to open cholecystectomy and biliary injuries.
long_answer: Patients with AC are more likely to undergo successful LC if cared for by a surgeon with an interest in laparoscopy. However, length of hospital stay is influenced more by patient factors in a multivariate model.

model_explanation: Yes, older adults with cancer are at a higher risk of falling. A longitudinal study found that older adults with cancer reported falls at a rate of 33%, compared to 29% without cancer (p<0.00). The study also showed that those with a history of cancer were more likely to fall than those without cancer, but no differences in fall rates were determined by cancer type or stage. This suggests that older adults with cancer are more prone to falls due to their underlying health condition rather than the type or progression of their cancer.
long_answer: The fall rate was higher in older adults with cancer than in older adults without cancer.

model_explanation: According to the two-year follow-up survey, the prognosis of occupational contact dermatitis from ubiquitous allergens (such as rubber chemicals and latex) is generally poor. In contrast, patients allergic to non-ubiquitous allergen epoxy tend to have a better prognosis, with higher rates of eczema clearance (22%) compared to those with ubiquituous allergy (10%). The study also found that job change was significantly associated with improvement in skin-related quality of life. Overall, the presence or absence of an omnipresent allergen appears to influence the prognosis of occupational contact dermatitis.
long_answer: At follow-up, patients with contact urticaria had significantly poorer prognosis than those with contact allergy, and there was a trend towards a poorer prognosis for those with contact allergy to rubber chemicals than those with allergy to epoxy. A significant positive association between job change and improvement was found.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, a subset of patients with prostate cancer (20%) developed metastatic disease, which was associated with significantly reduced overall survival rates. However, patients with 5 or fewer metastases had superior survival rates compared to those with more than 5 lesions (73% vs. 45% at 5 years). This suggests that there may be a favorable subset of patients who develop oligometastases, potentially with better prognosis and survival outcomes, although the exact characteristics of this subgroup are not specified in the study. Further research is needed to identify these patients.
long_answer: Patients with<or =5 metastatic sites had significantly better survival rates than patients with>5 lesions. Because existing sites of metastatic disease may be the primary sites of origin for additional metastases, our findings suggest that early detection and aggressive treatment of patients with a small number of metastatic lesions is worth testing as an approach to improving long-term survival.

model_explanation: Yes, radiotherapy (RT) around the time of pregnancy for Hodgkin's disease modifies the risk of breast cancer. A study found that women who received RT during or shortly after pregnancy had a significantly higher risk of developing secondary breast cancer compared to those not pregnant at the time of treatment (hazard ratio 22.49). The increased risk was dependent on the length of time from pregnancy to RT, with the highest risk observed for those irradiated during or within one month of pregnancy. This highlights the need for careful consideration in managing breast tissue during this period.
long_answer: The results of this study indicate that the risk of breast cancer after RT is greater with irradiation around the time of pregnancy. This suggests that pregnancy is a time of increased sensitivity of breast tissue to the carcinogenic effects of radiation. Because of the small sample size and limited follow-up, additional studies are recommended to confirm these findings.

model_explanation: According to the retrieved evidence, LAA occlusion devices do alter some echocardiography and ECG parameters in patients with atrial fibrillation. Slight and measureable movement of QRS electric axis was observed after device implantation. Significant differences were also seen in heart rate (HR) and mean QT interval between pre- and post-operation. However, no significant difference was found in echocardiographic parameters like left atrial diameter and aortic root diameter during follow-up visits. These changes suggest that LAA occlusion devices may have some impact on cardiac electrical activity but not necessarily on left atrial size.
long_answer: LAA occlusion device resulted in a slightly movement in QRS axis, reduced HR and increased the mean-mean QT interval duration. In addition, LA diameter and ARD seemed to be larger after device implantation.

model_explanation: Yes, non-invasive diagnosis of esophageal varices in patients with compensated hepatic cirrhosis is possible by duplex Doppler ultrasonography. The study found that mean portal vein velocity (PVV), splenic index (SI), and splenoportal index (SPI) were predictive of the presence of esophageal varices, with SPI being the most accurate parameter. A cut-off value of SPI at 5.0 offered high diagnostic accuracy (88%) for detecting esophageal varices without invasive screening endoscopy. This non-invasive method can help identify patients with compensated cirrhosis at risk for esophageal varix development.
long_answer: The SPI was accurate in predicting the presence or absence of esophageal varices in patients with compensated cirrhosis.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, the prevalence and hospital admission rates for asthma in children treated with different classes of medications were compared between two regions (Kuopio and Oulu provinces). While cromones had a higher proportion of readmissions (19.3%) compared to Oulu province averages, the differences in total and first admissions, as well as hospital days, were less prominent among children treated with cromones versus inhaled steroids. This suggests that while there may be some variation in treatment outcomes depending on medication choice, the differences are relatively small and not significantly different between the two groups.
long_answer: Our results suggest that inhaled steroids are better than cromones in preventing admissions for asthma when two provinces with different practices for maintenance medication of steady-state asthma were compared.

model_explanation: Yes, airway surgery appears to lower serum lipid levels in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) patients. A retrospective review of 113 adult OSA patients who underwent upper airway surgery found significant decreases in serum total cholesterol (TC), low-density lipoprotein particle number (LDL), and lipoprotein(a) [LP(a)] levels post-operatively compared to pre-operative levels. These changes were observed regardless of the type of surgery performed or baseline lipid status. The magnitude of lipid reductions varied by subgroup, but overall, airway surgery was associated with significant improvements in serum lipid profiles in OSA patients.
long_answer: Surgery may improve blood lipid levels in patients with OSA, especially in patients with preoperative dyslipidemia, potentially yielding a major benefit in metabolism and cardiovascular sequelae. Prospective studies should examine this potential metabolic effect of airway surgery for OSA.

model_explanation: The current readiness guidelines for hospitals in Israel are based on a 20% bed capacity threshold to accommodate multiple casualties. However, the study's results show that this guideline is not sufficient, as only 52% of HMCIs exceeded this capacity. The mean number of arriving casualties per hospital was significantly higher than anticipated (20.8). Predicting surge capacity and injury severity distribution could be improved by refining guidelines to account for higher-than-expected casualty loads and more severe injuries. This would help hospitals better prepare for HMCI events and reduce mortality rates.
long_answer: Hospital preparedness can be better defined by a fixed number of casualties rather than a percentile of its bed capacity. Only 20% of the arriving casualties will require immediate medical treatment. Implementation of this concept may improve the utilisation of national emergency health resources both in the preparation phase and on real time.

model_explanation: Yes, instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) can help predict dementia. A multicenter prospective cohort study found that participants with IADL disabilities at baseline had a higher conversion rate to dementia at 1- and 2-year follow-up compared to those without IADL disabilities. Structural equation modeling showed that IADL disability was associated with an increased risk of dementia, with odds ratios (OR) of 2.20 and 2.11 at 1- and 2-year follow-up, respectively. This suggests that measuring IADLs can be a useful tool in helping to predict the development of dementia.
long_answer: IADL disability is a useful addition to the diagnostic process in a memory clinic setting, indicating who is at higher risk of developing dementia at 1- and 2-year follow-up.

model_explanation: Yes, pelvic pain is significantly associated with defecatory symptoms in women with pelvic organ prolapse. A cross-sectional study of 248 women found that women with stage II or greater POP reported higher rates of defecatory symptoms such as straining with bowel movement, sense of incomplete emptying, and pain with bowel movement compared to those without pain. The odds ratios for these associations were 2.4, 4.4, 5.3, and 3.8, respectively. This suggests a strong link between pelvic pain and defecatory symptoms in women with POP.
long_answer: In women with POP, the symptom of pelvic pain is associated with the presence of defecatory symptoms.

model_explanation: The Symptom Checklist 90-R Obsessive-Compulsive subscale (SCL 90-R OC) is related to symptoms of depression, anxiety, and subjective complaints of memory problems. While it does not directly relate to objective measures of attention or verbal memory, it significantly correlates with reported symptoms of depression and anxiety. This suggests that the SCL 90-R OC may identify cognitive impairments associated with these mental health conditions. However, its predictive power is limited compared to other factors, as symptoms of depression contribute a significant portion of the variance in predicting SCL 90-R OC scores.
long_answer: Our data suggest that the SCL 90-R is best viewed as an indicator of unidimensional emotional distress and somatic effects of structural brain injury.

model_explanation: Yes, based on the retrieved evidence, non-HDL-cholesterol appears to be a better predictor of long-term outcome in patients after acute myocardial infarction compared to LDL-cholesterol. A study published in Thailand found that patients with non-HDL-C >130 mg/dl had a higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) compared to those with non-HDL-C <100 mg/dl. In contrast, LDL-C >100 mg/dl was associated with reduced risk of MACE. This suggests that targeting non-HDL-cholesterol may be more effective in preventing long-term cardiovascular outcomes than targeting LDL-cholesterol.
long_answer: Non-attaining non-HDL-C goal predicted MACE at long-term follow-up after AMI whereas non-attaining LDL-C goal was not associated with the higher risk. Therefore, non-HDL-C may be a more suitable target of dyslipidemia treatment than LDL-C in patients after AMI.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, diffusion-weighted (DW) MR imaging offers additional incremental value to conventional nonenhanced MR images in detecting uterine endometrial cancer. DW images detected cancers in 96% of patients, including those not visible on T2-weighted images. The apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values were also significantly lower for endometrial cancer compared to normal endometrium and other tissues. While sensitivity was highest for lesions appearing hyperintense or hypointense on DW images, the overall detection value of DW imaging alone was 96%, indicating its usefulness in enhancing cancer detection in nonenhanced MR imaging.
long_answer: DW imaging can be helpful in the detection of uterine endometrial cancer in nonenhanced MR imaging.

model_explanation: Yes, pediatric housestaff experience influences tests ordered for infants in the neonatal intensive care unit. A prospective cohort study found that interns ordered significantly more arterial blood gases per infant (3.22 vs. 2.89) and $169 more at a particular institution compared to residents. There was no difference in radiographs or electrolytes ordered between interns and residents. This suggests that housestaff experience may impact the number of tests ordered, potentially due to differences in clinical confidence or decision-making. However, further studies are needed to fully understand this relationship.
long_answer: Interns order significantly more arterial blood gases per infant than junior and senior residents on-call in the neonatal ICU. Additional study is required to see if the experience of housestaff is associated with a broader array of neonatal outcomes, such as morbidity and mortality.

model_explanation: Biomolecular identification of allergenic pollen using real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and fluoro-immunoassay offers a promising alternative to traditional morphologic analysis. This approach provides rapid, accurate, and automated detection and quantification of airborne allergenic pollen taxa. The modified DNA extraction protocol and developed TaqMan probes enable proper identification of pollen even when collected on routine aerobiological tape. The ImmunoCAP ISAC 112 fluoro-immunoassay shows high reliability in intra- and inter-assay analysis, with good agreement across laboratories. This new perspective has the potential to enhance aerobiological monitoring for allergy patients.
long_answer: The real-time PCR approach revealed promising results in pollen identification and quantification, even when analyzing pollen mixes. Future perspectives could concern the development of multiplex real-time PCR for the simultaneous detection of different taxa in the same reaction tube and the application of high-throughput molecular methods.

model_explanation: The suitability of the revised node staging (seventh TNM) as a biological predictor for early gastric cancer is not definitively established. The analysis suggests that certain clinicopathological factors, such as poor differentiation, perineural invasion, and larger size, are more significantly associated with higher stage in both mucosal and submucosal cancers. However, the revised staging system does not provide clear correlations between these factors and biological behavior. Therefore, it is unclear whether the seventh TNM edition can reliably predict the clinical behavior of early gastric cancer based on current evidence.
long_answer: Upstaging in EGC based on the revised TNM staging reflects more aggressive biological behavior of cancer. The new TNM staging system may be informative in prediction of biological behavior of EGC as well as prognosis and survival.

model_explanation: Lower fasting plasma glucose (FPG) levels at diagnosis of type 2 diabetes are associated with improved outcomes. The U.K. Diabetes Prospective Study found that individuals with FPG below 140 mg/dl (<7.8 mmol/l) had a reduced risk for diabetic complications, whereas those with intermediate and high FPG levels had higher risks. Additionally, the study showed that individuals in lower FPG groups had significantly reduced risks for progression of retinopathy, reduction in vibration sensory threshold, or development of microalbuminuria compared to those in higher FPG groups.
long_answer: People presenting with type 2 diabetes with lower initial glycemia who may be earlier in the course of their disease had fewer adverse clinical outcomes despite similar glycemic progression. Since most such people are asymptomatic at diagnosis, active case detection programs would be required to identify them.

model_explanation: Remote ischemic postconditioning (RIPC) has been shown to partially protect against myocardial damage associated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Studies suggest that RIPC can reduce myocardial lesions and improve outcomes in patients undergoing elective PCI for stable angina or non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome. However, the protective effect may be less pronounced in diabetic patients. While results are promising, more research is needed to fully understand its benefits and potential limitations in this context.
long_answer: This clinical trial evaluated the possible reduction in intervention-related myocardial damage that was attributable to remote postischemic conditioning.

model_explanation: Yes, based on the retrieved evidence, multi-modal cervical physical therapy appears to be effective in improving tinnitus complaints in patients with cervicogenic somatic tinnitus (CST). A randomized controlled trial found significant improvements in Tinnitus Functional Index (TFI) and Neck Bournemouth Questionnaire (NBQ) scores after 6 weeks of treatment, with substantial improvement reported by 53% of patients immediately after treatment. The effect was maintained in 24% of patients at follow-up. While no experimental studies were available prior to this trial, the results suggest that multi-modal cervical physical therapy may be a beneficial treatment for CST.
long_answer: Cervical physical therapy can have a positive effect on subjective tinnitus complaints in patients with a combination of tinnitus and neck complaints. Larger studies, using more responsive outcome measures, are however necessary to prove this effect.

model_explanation: The evidence suggests that the content and presentation of participant information sheets can influence perceptions and behavior. For example, pregnant women rated the Double Awkward condition as significantly more complex than the Double Fluent condition, indicating that clear and fluent language can improve understanding. Additionally, a study on postpartum care found that women's concerns and unmet learning needs changed over time, with those of low socioeconomic status reporting more unmet needs. These findings suggest that effective information presentation is crucial for recruitment and participation in interventions.
long_answer: Font influenced pregnant women's ratings of intervention complexity.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, the training of Ophthalmologist Diplomats (ODTs) in West Africa can be improved. While TODs generally reported satisfaction with the program and felt well-structured, there were areas for improvement, including inadequate sponsorship, short duration of the course, and poor accommodation facilities. Increasing training posts, training allowances, and incentives for trainers/training hospitals could address these issues. Additionally, improving the overall structure and support systems for ODTs may enhance their abilities to strengthen healthcare systems in low- and middle-income countries. More comprehensive evaluations are necessary to inform improvements.
long_answer: The ODT programme ensures ophthalmic manpower for secondary eye care level despite challenges. The stakeholders should look into problems facing the programme in order to improve it.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, triage nurses' predictions of admission were not significantly different from GAPS (a machine learning algorithm) predictions. However, when nurses felt certain of their prediction (>95%), their accuracy was excellent (92.4%). In contrast, GAPS outperformed VAS (visual analogue scale) in calibration (+1.2% vs +9.2%, p<0.0001), discrimination (AUC 0.810 vs 0.759, p=0.001), and accuracy (75.1% vs 68.9%, p=0.0009). GAPS also performed well when combining with clinical certainty (>95%). Overall, while nurses' subjective predictions have value, a simple objective score like GAPS may be more accurate in predicting admission.
long_answer: GAPS, a simple clinical score, is a better predictor of admission than triage nurses, unless the nurse is sure about the outcome, in which case their clinical judgement should be respected.

model_explanation: Yes, adult body circumferences are associated with height. According to Evidence 1, when adjusted for age and race, waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference (HC) scaled to height with powers of 0.76 ± 0.08 and 0.45 ± 0.05 in men, and 0.80 ± 0.05 and 0.53 ± 0.04 in women, respectively (all P<0.001). This suggests that as height increases, WC and HC also increase proportionally. The scaling of body mass index to height was also examined, with weight scaling to a power of 2.29 in men and 1.80 in women.
long_answer: Circumferences and related ratios scale significantly to height, notably after adjustment for age and race, across subjects who are representative of the US population. These observations have implications for the clinical and epidemiologic use of these anthropometric measures and indexes.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, the progression rate of valvar aortic stenosis can be predicted with reasonable accuracy. The degree of valvar calcification and aortic valve opening area (AVA) are found to be exponentially correlated with the progression of aortic stenosis. The study provides specific criteria for assessing rapid hemodynamic progression, including AVA values that indicate the need for surgical intervention. With these criteria, healthcare providers can accurately predict when patients with valvar aortic stenosis require surgical intervention. This allows for timely management and potentially improved outcomes.
long_answer: The present data indicate that for clinical purposes and planning of valvar surgery the progression of asymptomatic aortic stenosis can be sufficiently predicted by the present aortic valve opening area and the degree of valvar calcification.

model_explanation: The National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) does not favor left hemisphere strokes. In fact, the study suggests that patients with right hemisphere strokes tend to have larger infarct volumes compared to those with left hemisphere strokes, even when adjusting for NIHSS scores. The median volume of a right hemisphere stroke was roughly double the median volume of a left hemisphere stroke in patients with similar NIHSS scores. This implies that the NIHSS may not specifically favor one hemisphere over the other, but rather reflects the severity of neurological deficit regardless of the infarct location.
long_answer: For a given NIHSS score, the median volume of right hemisphere strokes is consistently larger than the median volume of left hemisphere strokes. The clinical implications of our finding need further exploration.

model_explanation: The adenoma detection rate (ADR) was significantly higher with Golytely compared to MiraLAX. In the post-hoc analysis of an RCT, the ADR with Golytely was 26.2% (27/103), whereas with MiraLAX it was 16.1% (14/87). Although the difference was not statistically significant (P=0.091), multivariate analyses suggested that Golytely was 2.28 times more likely to be associated with adenoma detection than MiraLAX, indicating a higher adenoma detection rate with Golytely. However, the difference did not reach statistical significance at the univariate level.
long_answer: Golytely was more efficacious than MiraLAX in bowel cleansing, and was independently associated with both bowel prep quality (BBPS ≥ 7) and higher adenoma detection. Golytely should be used as first line for bowel prep for colonoscopy. Studies with larger populations are needed to confirm these results.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, it appears that gingival crevicular blood can be used as an alternative method to assess blood glucose levels. The observational cross-sectional study found a strong correlation between gingival crevicular blood and finger-prick blood, with a t value of 3.97 (P value = 0.001). Additionally, another study reported that patients with periodontitis were more likely to have undiagnosed diabetes mellitus, suggesting that this method could be useful for early detection. However, further research is needed to confirm its reliability and accuracy in clinical settings.
long_answer: The data from this study has shown that GCB collected during diagnostic periodontal examination can be an excellent source of blood for glucometric analysis.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, the implementation of evidence-based measures for catheter care led to a significant reduction in central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI) rates from 4.1 per 1000 line days in 2009 to zero for >370 consecutive days in 2012 and then again maintained at zero for >600 days after a series of interventions. This suggests that a zero CLABSI rate is not only achievable but also sustainable with ongoing training, surveillance, and vigilance with catheter insertion and maintenance practices and improved documentation. The sustainability of this achievement appears to be confirmed over time.
long_answer: High-quality training, strict compliance with evidence-based guidelines, and thorough documentation is associated with significant reductions in CLABSIs. Mindful organizing may lead to a better understanding of what goes into a unit's ability to handle peak demands and sustain extraordinary performance in the long-term.

model_explanation: Yes, treatment duration affects outcome after radiotherapy for prostate cancer. A study evaluating patients with prostate cancer treated with radiotherapy found that patients who had shorter treatment durations (NTDR < 33%) had higher 10-year freedom from biochemical failure rates compared to those with longer treatment durations (NTDR ≥ 33%). Another study also showed that shorter metastatic disease, including fewer than 5 lesions, was associated with improved overall survival and metastasis-free survival rates. These findings suggest that shorter treatment duration may be beneficial for prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy.
long_answer: A proportionally longer treatment duration was identified as an adverse factor in low-risk patients. Treatment breaks resulting in a NTDR of>/=33% (e.g., four or more breaks during a 40-fraction treatment, 5 d/wk) should be avoided.

model_explanation: The concept of patient-controlled therapy (PCT) for breathlessness in palliative care is promising. The pilot observational study suggests that intravenous opioid PCT can effectively reduce breathlessness symptoms in patients with advanced disease and refractory breathlessness. Secondary aims of feasibility and acceptance were met, with 12/18 patients reporting relief from breathlessness on Day 3. While more research is needed, the results provide a basis for exploring PCT as an additional treatment option for managing breathlessness in palliative care. Further studies are necessary to fully evaluate its efficacy and potential benefits.
long_answer: Opioid PCT is a feasible and acceptable therapeutic method to reduce refractory breathlessness in palliative care patients.

model_explanation: Yes, pain is a clinically relevant problem in general adult psychiatry. The study found that nearly 75% of patients with psychiatric disorders experience pain, and those with affective disorders are most frequently affected. Pain is associated with impairment, unfitness for work, and depression, indicating its significant impact on mental health treatment outcomes. Furthermore, the study suggests that hospice residents receiving regular treatment for daily pain have a lower risk of mortality compared to non-hospice residents, highlighting the importance of pain management in palliative care.
long_answer: We found evidence that pain can be a significant clinical problem in psychiatric patients which seems to be underestimated in psychiatry. The investigated patients in general adult psychiatry are characterized by specific risk factors different from clinical subpopulations of other disciplines.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, the current consensus suggests that operative treatment for displaced midshaft clavicular fractures (DMCF) is superior to nonoperative treatment in terms of rates of nonunion, malunion, and overall complications. However, subgroup analyses reveal significant differences in incidence of neurologic symptoms and dissatisfaction with appearance between surgical and non-surgical groups. Additionally, functional outcomes were significantly improved with operative treatment. Therefore, the evidence suggests that surgically treating DMCF may be beneficial for most patients, but further research is needed to determine the optimal treatment approach for individual cases.
long_answer: The available evidence suggests that the operative treatment for DMCF is associated with a lower rate of nonunion, malunion and complication than nonoperative treatment. This study supports traditional primary operative treatment for DMCF in active adults.

model_explanation: The evidence suggests that technology alone, such as insulin dose advisors (IDAs) and telemonitoring/teleconsultation functions, may not be sufficient to improve glycemic control for type 1 diabetes. While IDAs improved glycemic control in patients who used them regularly, the improvement was more significant in those receiving support via teleconsultation. Additionally, a study on type 2 diabetes found that technology had limited impact on glycemic control, with no significant difference between high, intermediate, and low fasting plasma glucose levels at diagnosis. Thus, technology may be only one part of a comprehensive approach to improving glycemic control.
long_answer: The Diabeo system improved glycaemic control in both high and low users who avidly used the IDA function, while the greatest improvement was seen in the low users who had the motivational support of teleconsultations.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, individuals with type 1 diabetes do not necessarily consume a high atherogenic diet. A 7-year cohort study found minor changes in nutrient intake, including lower protein and fat intakes, but higher carbohydrate and fibre intakes compared to European nutritional recommendations. Additionally, they followed dietary guidelines for protein, fat, carbohydrate, cholesterol, but not for fibre and saturated fat. This suggests that the majority of individuals with type 1 diabetes do follow a relatively balanced diet according to current European nutritional recommendations.
long_answer: European individuals with type 1 diabetes consume a high atherogenic diet as few patients met recommendations for dietary fibre and saturated fat. This study showed minor changes in dietary nutrients and energy intakes over a period of 7 years. Nutrition education needs particular focus on strategies to increase dietary fibre and reduce saturated fat to exploit their potential benefit.

model_explanation: According to the retrieved evidence, preoperative platelet count in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is indeed a prognostic factor. A study found that patients with a platelet count ≤ 205 had a significantly better 5-year survival rate compared to those with >205, especially when nodes were involved. Multivariate analysis also confirmed that platelet count was an independent prognostic factor, along with T grade and N staging. This suggests that preoperative platelet count can provide valuable information on prognosis for ESCC patients.
long_answer: Preoperative platelet count is a predictive factor for long-term survival in ESCC, especially in nodal-positive patients. We conclude that 205 (×10(9)/L) may be the optimum cutoff point for platelet count in predicting survival in ESCC patients.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, serum pancreatic lipase may replace serum amylase as a biomarker for acute pancreatitis. The area under the curve (AUC) analysis showed improved diagnostic accuracy for serum pancreatic lipase compared to serum amylase (0.948 vs. 0.906). Additionally, serum pancreatic lipase had a higher sensitivity and specificity in detecting acute pancreatitis, with lower false negatives and false positives compared to serum amylase. The study suggests that serum pancreatic lipase may be more reliable and useful in diagnosing acute pancreatitis than serum amylase.
long_answer: It is concluded that serum pancreatic lipase is a more accurate biomarker of acute pancreatitis than serum amylase.

model_explanation: Yes, electrochemiluminescence (ECL) assays can improve prediction of time to type 1 diabetes in autoantibody-positive TrialNet subjects. A multivariate Cox proportional hazards model with ECL positivity and other factors remained significantly associated with time to diabetes. Adding ECL to the Diabetes Prevention Trial risk score (DPTRS) improved receiver operating characteristic curves, resulting in an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83, indicating better predictive accuracy. This suggests that ECL assays can be a valuable tool in predicting the progression to type 1 diabetes in individuals with autoantibodies.
long_answer: ECL assays improved the ability to predict time to diabetes in these autoantibody-positive relatives at risk for developing diabetes. These findings might be helpful in the design and eligibility criteria for prevention trials in the future.

model_explanation: According to the evidence, yes, the SYNTAX score (SxS) predicts in-hospital outcomes for patients with ST elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI). The study found that patients with high SxS (>22) had higher rates of no-reflow, lower ejection fraction, reinfarction, and mortality during hospitalization compared to those with low SxS (<22). On multivariate logistic regression analysis, SxS was an independent predictor of no-reflow. The study suggests that SxS can be used as a prognostic tool for predicting in-hospital outcomes in STEMI patients undergoing pPCI.
long_answer: SxS is a useful tool that can predict in-hospital outcomes of patients with STEMI undergoing pPCI.

model_explanation: According to the retrieved evidence, behavioral risk factors may play a significant role in the conversion from optimal blood pressure to hypertensive status among Black South Africans. The Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology study found that African individuals with optimal blood pressure who became hypertensive smoked more and had greater waist circumference, γ-glutamyltransferase levels, and higher alcohol intake compared to those who remained normotensive. Additionally, HIV infection was inversely associated with increased blood pressure in this population. Therefore, behavioral modifications, such as smoking cessation and weight management, may be crucial in preventing the development of hypertension in Black South Africans.
long_answer: During the 5 years, 24% of Africans with optimal BP developed hypertension. The surge in hypertension in Africa is largely explained by modifiable risk factors. Public health strategies should focus aggressively on lifestyle to prevent a catastrophic burden on the national health system.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 2, the type of tibial component used can significantly impact mechanical alignment in unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR). Patients who received an all-polyethylene inlay component had a greater mean postoperative mechanical alignment correction (mean=2.8°) compared to those with a metal-backed onlay component (mean=3.9°). The thickness of the tibial polyethylene insert also had a significant effect on postoperative alignment. This suggests that choosing the right type and design of tibial component is crucial for achieving optimal mechanical alignment in UKR.
long_answer: Patients who received a metal-backed Onlay tibial component obtained better postoperative mechanical alignment compared to those who received all-polyethylene Inlay prostheses. The thicker overall construct of Onlay prostheses appears to be an important determinant of postoperative alignment. Considering their higher survivorship rates and improved postoperative mechanical alignment, Onlay prostheses should be the first option when performing medial UKR.

model_explanation: Yes, the Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program appears to reduce disability in the elderly. According to Evidence 1, a $100 per month increase in maximum SSI benefits led to a 0.46 percentage point decrease in mobility limitations among single elderly individuals, with robust findings across sensitivity analyses and subgroups. This suggests that increasing SSI benefits may improve health outcomes for vulnerable elderly populations. While the evidence is limited to SSI recipients, it supports the idea that income support policies can have a positive impact on population health.
long_answer: Income support policy may be a significant new lever for improving population health, especially that of lower-income persons. Even though the findings are robust, further analyses are needed to confirm their reliability. Future research should examine a variety of different income support policies, as well as whether a broader range of social and economic policies affect health.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, yes, serum can be used as an alternative to tumor tissue for analyzing EGFR mutation status. The study found that there was a high correlation (correlation index 0.62; P<0.001) between the mutations detected in serum samples and those detected in matched tumor samples. Additionally, EGFR mutations were detectable in serum samples of 11 patients out of 57 pairs (19.3%), while they were detectable in tumor samples of 12 patients. This suggests that serum can be a valuable tool for analyzing EGFR mutation status in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer.
long_answer: Serum sample might be alternatively used in the difficult time of getting tumor tissue for analyzing the status of EGFR mutation status in patients with advanced NSCLC.

model_explanation: Yes, failures of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) are associated with steep posterior tibial slopes. A study found that patients who experienced ACLR failure had significantly steeper medial and lateral posterior tibial slopes compared to those without ACLR failure or controls. Specifically, the median posterior tibial slope was 3.5° ± 2.5° for ACLR failure group (medial) and 2.9° ± 2.1° for ACLR failure group (lateral), which were significantly steeper than the controls (6.1° ± 2.1° and 5.5° ± 3.0°, respectively).
long_answer: Both medial and lateral PTS were significantly steeper in failures of ACLR than the control group. Medial or lateral PTS ≥5° was a new risk factor of ACLR failure.

model_explanation: The retrieved evidence suggests that teleoncology models of care can enable the safe delivery of chemotherapy in rural towns. The comparison study between Mount Isa and Townsville Cancer Centre found similar toxicity rates and dose intensities for patients treated via teleoncology versus those at a tertiary cancer centre, with no significant differences in demographic characteristics or hospital admissions. Additionally, the retrospective audit of patients with metastatic colorectal and node-positive breast cancers also showed comparable profiles of serious adverse events between urban and rural patients. This supports the effectiveness of teleoncology models in providing equal care to rural populations.
long_answer: It appears safe to administer chemotherapy in rural towns under the supervision of medical oncologists from larger centres via teleoncology, provided that rural health care resources and governance arrangements are adequate.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, a solitary kidney may be more resistant to warm ischemia compared to paired kidneys. In one study, dogs with a solitary kidney (group 1) showed a decrease in clearance of 20% at 1 week but regained basal function by week 2, whereas dogs with both kidneys (group 2) experienced a 90% decrease in clearance up to week 2 and only started recovering at week 3. Histopathological examination also revealed less severe tubular necrosis in group 1 compared to group 2.
long_answer: Solitary kidney in a canine model is more resistant to ischemia than paired kidneys based on radiological, pathological and genetic evidence.

model_explanation: Based on the provided evidence, performing rectal anastomosis in gynaecological debulking surgery without a diverting stoma appears to be safe. The first study shows that 43 patients underwent colorectal procedures without significant complications or anastomotic leakage when using a diverting stoma. The second study found no difference in clinical effects, morbidity, or stoma requirement between patients with restorative proctocolectomy and those with ileorectal anastomosis who developed desmoids. The third study showed that patients with anastomotic leakage had similar continence function and sphincter function as those without complications.
long_answer: Low rectal resection during debulking procedures for gynaecological cancers with peritoneal carcinomatosis can safely be performed by an experienced surgeon without a diverting stoma.

model_explanation: Yes, the Mammography Quality Standards Act has had an impact on improving mammography quality in North Carolina. The study found that between the first and second inspections (1995), the percentage of facilities meeting quality standards increased: phantom scores passing rate from 31.6% to 78.2%, darkroom fog passing rate from 74.3% to 88.5%, and temperature difference passing rate from 62.4% to 86.9%. This suggests that federal regulations have led to improved mammography quality in North Carolina, indicating a positive effect of the Mammography Quality Standards Act on mammography practices.
long_answer: In 1995, the first year that the MQSA was in effect, there was a significant improvement in the quality of mammography in North Carolina. This improvement probably resulted from facilities' compliance with federal regulations.

model_explanation: The evidence suggests that breast cancer prognosis may have an hereditary component. A population-based cohort study found that daughters and sisters of women with poor breast cancer prognosis had a higher risk of mortality compared to those with good prognosis (HR, 1.6; p = 0.002). Another study using BRCA mutation carriers showed that genetic susceptibility SNPs improved predictive ability of risk models for survival. A third study analyzing recurrent breast cancer found that more recent cohorts had longer survival. These findings suggest a possible inherited component to breast cancer prognosis, but more research is needed to confirm this.
long_answer: Breast cancer prognosis of a woman predicts the survival in her first-degree relatives with breast cancer. Our novel findings suggest that breast cancer prognosis might be inherited.

model_explanation: Yes, c-kit is a potential therapeutic target for treating uveal melanoma. The study found that c-kit was strongly expressed and tyrosine phosphorylated in cultured uveal melanoma cells, suggesting its involvement in cell growth and survival. Treatment with STI571, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor that blocks c-kit autophosphorylation, resulted in cell death, with an IC50 of less than 2.5 microM. This suggests that targeting the c-kit pathway may provide a potential therapeutic strategy for uveal melanoma treatment.
long_answer: The results confirm that c-kit is vastly expressed in uveal melanoma, suggest that the c-kit molecular pathway may be important in uveal melanoma growth, and point to its use as a target for therapy with STI571.

model_explanation: According to the retrieved evidence, pituitary apoplexy's histological features did not significantly influence its clinical presentation or outcome. A retrospective analysis of 59 patients with pituitary apoplexy showed that patients with infarction alone had similar outcomes to those with hemorrhagic infarction and/or frank hemorrhage. The presenting symptoms, endocrinological status, and outcome were comparable between the two groups. However, certain clinical features such as tumor location at surgery did influence the outcome, with tumors identified during surgery having a higher remission rate compared to those not identified.
long_answer: The patients who presented with histological features of pituitary tumor infarction alone had less severe clinical features on presentation, a longer course prior to presentation, and a better outcome than those presenting with hemorrhagic infarction or frank hemorrhage. The endocrine replacement requirements were similar in both groups.

model_explanation: Yes, orthostatic myoclonus (OM) is an underrecognized cause of unsteadiness. Studies have shown that OM is present in approximately 17-20% of patients with unexplained gait impairment and unsteadiness. OM is associated with various neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple system atrophy, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease. The condition can be improved with antimyoclonic treatment, but follow-up periods are often insufficient to evaluate its therapeutic effect. As a result, OM may be underrecognized or misattributed to other conditions, highlighting the need for increased awareness and diagnostic consideration in clinical practice.
long_answer: Orthostatic myoclonus is often underdiagnosed and can be considered a possible cause of unsteadiness in subjects with neurodegenerative diseases. Electromyography surface recording is thereby an aid for investigating unsteadiness of unknown origin.

model_explanation: Yes, based on the evidence. Serum chloride levels below 100 mmol/l were found to be associated with increased risks of total and cardiovascular disease mortalities in both men and women. The risk ratio was particularly high for women (2.16), indicating that low serum chloride levels may be a significant risk factor for cardiovascular mortality in this population, independent of other factors such as age, sex, and body mass index. This association was observed even after adjusting for other serum electrolytes and confounding variables.
long_answer: This s the first report from a population-based study to indicate that there is an association between serum chloride level and the incidence of total, CVD and non-CVD mortalities. The risk ratio for CVD mortality associated with a low serum chloride level was comparable to or higher than those observed for well-established CVD risk factors.

model_explanation: Yes, ethnicity appears to affect where people with cancer die. According to Evidence 1, mortality data from London showed that deaths in hospital declined while home deaths increased among BAME groups over time. Adjusting for other factors, hospital deaths were more likely for those born in Asia and Africa, while hospice deaths were less likely for these groups. Similarly, evidence suggests that geographic regions with significant racial disparities in breast cancer mortality tend to have higher poverty rates. These findings suggest that ethnicity may influence the place of death among people with cancer.
long_answer: Location of death varies by country of birth. BAME groups are more likely to die in a hospital and less likely to die at home or in a hospice. Further investigation is needed to determine whether these differences result from patient-centred preferences, or other environment or service-related factors. This knowledge will enable strategies to be developed to improve access to relevant palliative care and related services, where necessary.

model_explanation: The study suggests that transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) is a reliable tool to assess left ventricular function in brain-dead donors. Fifty-five potential heart donors were evaluated using TEE before harvesting, and 36 hearts were successfully transplanted. The results showed that even hearts with an Fractional Area Change (FAC) of less than 50% can be suitable for transplantation if the recipient is alive, not retransplanted, without assistance devices or epinephrine infusions above 1 mg/h and shows an ejection fraction above 40%. This expands the donor pool for heart transplantation.
long_answer: TEE is useful to assess left ventricular function in potential brain-dead donors. An FAC less than 50% is present in 36% of potential heart donors. Because left ventricular dysfunction is often reversible shortly after transplantation, an FAC below 50% may not necessarily preclude the use of hearts for transplantation.

model_explanation: Yes, based on the retrieved evidence, the postoperative pain level can be predicted preoperatively. Studies have shown that factors such as past history of pain, intensity and duration of prior pain, triggering factors, localization, and psychological context can predict postoperative pain intensity. Specifically, significant preoperative pain and depression are associated with increased risk of intense postoperative pain. Additionally, patients with a prior history of surgical pain or those who experience severe pain before surgery are more likely to have intense postoperative pain. These findings suggest that preoperative assessment can help predict postoperative pain levels.
long_answer: Significant postoperative pain can be expected in the following situations: pain after prior surgery, presence of chronic pain sustained for more than six months, intense preoperative pain, state of depression.

model_explanation: The retrieved evidence does not directly address whether age moderates the effect of personality disorder on coping style in psychiatric inpatients. However, Evidence 1 suggests that older adults reported less symptomatology and lower levels of dysfunctional coping strategies compared to younger patients with personality dysfunction. This implies that age may moderate the relationship between personality disorder and coping style, potentially due to changes in symptom presentation over the lifespan. Further investigation is needed to explore this hypothesis.
long_answer: This study found that influences on coping were multifactorial and moderated by age. These factors have implications for interventions designed to enhance coping strategies.

model_explanation: Yes, neck pain is associated with worse health-related quality of life (HRQoL) 6 months later. The study found an exposure-response relationship between neck pain and physical HRQoL after adjusting for confounding factors. Participants with mild, intense, or disabling neck pain at baseline had worse physical HRQoL 6 months later compared to those without neck pain. A worsening course of neck pain and persistent neck pain were also associated with worse physical HRQoL. However, no association was found between neck pain and mental HRQoL.
long_answer: We found that neck pain was negatively associated with physical but not mental HRQoL. Our analysis suggests that neck pain may be a contributor of future poor physical HRQoL in the population. Raising awareness of the possible future impact of neck pain on physical HRQoL is important for health-care providers and policy makers with respect to the management of neck pain in populations.

model_explanation: According to Evidence 1, there is a significant correlation between end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) and arterial carbon dioxide (PaCO2) in ventilated extremely low birth weight (ELBW) infants in the first week of life. The correlation coefficient was 0.81, indicating a strong agreement between the two measurements. The bias between EtCO2 and PaCO2 was 5.6 +/- 6.9 mmHg, but within a range of 30 to 50 mmHg, capnographic methods were able to identify 84% of instances where PaCO2 was between 35 and 55 mmHg.
long_answer: There is good correlation and agreement between end-tidal CO(2) and arterial CO(2) in ELBW infants in the EtCO(2) range 30-50 mmHg. End-tidal CO(2) monitoring can be helpful in trending or for screening abnormal PaCO(2) values in ELBW infants in first week of life.

model_explanation: The current evidence suggests that some pre-residency selection criteria may predict performance in orthopedic surgery residency. For instance, USMLE Step 2 scores and number of clinical clerkship honors were associated with objective measures such as ABOS Part I scores and OITE scores. Additionally, AOA membership was correlated with higher global evaluation scores. However, the association between pre-residency selection criteria and performance in orthopedic surgery residency is not strong, and subjective ratings by faculty remain a significant predictor of success. Further studies are needed to clarify the predictive value of pre-residency selection factors.
long_answer: We found that USMLE Step 2, number of honors in medical school clerkships, and AOA membership demonstrated the strongest correlations with resident performance. Our goal in analyzing these data was to provide residency programs at large a sense of which criteria may be "high yield" in ranking applicants by analyzing data from within our own pool of residents. Similar studies across a broader scope of programs are warranted to confirm applicability of our findings. The continually emerging complexities of the field of orthopaedic surgery lend increasing importance to future work on the appropriate selection and training of orthopaedic residents.

model_explanation: According to the retrieved evidence, yes, CA72-4 is a useful biomarker in differential diagnosis between ovarian endometrioma and epithelial ovarian cancer. A significant difference was observed in CA72-4 values between women with ovarian cancer (71.0%) and patients with endometriosis (13.8%) (P<0.0001). This suggests that CA72-4 may be a reliable marker to help distinguish between these two conditions, which can aid in accurate diagnosis and treatment planning for patients desiring pregnancy or without symptoms of ovarian cancer. It is not useful for discriminating ovarian endometrioma from ovarian malignancy due to high CA125 levels.
long_answer: This study suggests that CA72-4 determination can be useful to confirm the benign nature of ovarian endometriomas in women with high CA125 levels.

model_explanation: Based on the evidence, breastfeeding appears to be beneficial for children with a family history of atopy. The study found that breastfed children had lower rates of illness, including gastroenteritis, respiratory tract infections, and skin infections, compared to non-breastfed children. Additionally, another study suggested a correlation between atopic dermatitis and cutaneous infections such as impetigo contagiosum and molluscum contagiosum. While the evidence is not conclusive, breastfeeding may be a simple yet effective way to reduce the risk of illness in children with a family history of atopy.
long_answer: Our results suggest a protective effect of breast-feeding among children with a family history of atopy that is not confined to the period of breast-feeding but continues during the first three years of life. Breast-feeding should be promoted in children with a family history of atopy.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, bare-metal stent (BMS) implantation may still be justifiable in high bleeding risk patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), particularly when compared to zotarolimus-eluting endothelial stent (E-ZES). The ZEUS trial showed that E-ZES was associated with increased major adverse cardiovascular events and decreased composite stent thrombosis rates, while bleeding events did not differ between groups. In contrast, the evidence does not strongly support BMS as being superior to E-ZES in high bleeding risk patients. Therefore, individualized decision-making is necessary for each patient's specific circumstances.
long_answer: Among HBR patients with stable or unstable coronary artery disease, E-ZES implantation provides superior efficacy and safety as compared with conventional BMS. (Zotarolimus-Eluting Endeavor Sprint Stent in Uncertain DES Candidates [ZEUS]; NCT01385319).

model_explanation: The association between marital status, living arrangements, and mortality varies by gender. Men tend to benefit more from being married than women with respect to mortality in middle age. However, for older individuals, widowed individuals exhibit lower mortality rates compared to divorced and single individuals. For women, the highest mortality risk is observed for those who are single and living with a partner, whereas optimistic outlooks are associated with lower mortality risks across both sexes, regardless of marital status or living arrangements. The impact of marital status on mortality appears to decrease in older age groups.
long_answer: Evaluation of living arrangements is crucial for identifying and explaining gender differences in mortality risks by marital status. The impact of living alone and living with a partner seems to be different in men and women.

model_explanation: Yes, based on Evidence 1, ibuprofen increases perioperative blood loss associated with major orthopaedic surgery. The study found that patients pretreated with ibuprofen experienced a 45% increase in perioperative blood loss compared to those who received a placebo. Specifically, the total blood loss in the ibuprofen group was 1161 mL, while in the placebo group it was 796 mL. This suggests that ibuprofen may not be ideal for patients undergoing major orthopaedic surgery such as hip arthroplasty due to its potential to increase bleeding risk.
long_answer: Pretreatment with ibuprofen before elective total hip surgery increases the perioperative blood loss significantly. Early discontinuation of non-selective non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs is advised.

model_explanation: No, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alone cannot accurately predict concordant pain provocation during provocative disc injection. According to Evidence 1, while certain MRI findings such as disc protrusion with high intensity zone (HIZ) correlated significantly with concordant pain, other factors like disc degeneration and HIZ without disc contour abnormalities were not helpful in identifying discs with concordant pain. A combination analysis of HIZ and disc contour abnormalities was necessary to accurately predict concordant pain provocation. Therefore, MRI should be used as part of a comprehensive evaluation, rather than the sole diagnostic tool for predicting response to provocative disc injection.
long_answer: The proposed MR classification is useful to predict a disc with concordant pain. Disc protrusion with HIZ on MR imaging predicted positive discography in patients with discogenic low back pain.

model_explanation: Yes, case-mix based reimbursement appears to stimulate the development of process-oriented care delivery. According to Evidence 1, hospitals that adopted this type of reimbursement were more likely to establish care programmes using process-oriented performance measures. However, the implementation of these programmes was not accompanied by a shift from function-based to process-based care delivery. Instead, hospitals focused on improving efficiency without necessarily changing their underlying care processes. This suggests that case-mix based reimbursement can drive some changes in care delivery, but may not necessarily lead to a fundamental shift towards more coordinated and interconnected care.
long_answer: This study demonstrates that hospital management can stimulate the development of care programmes by the adoption of case-mix reimbursement within hospitals' budgeting processes. Future research is recommended to confirm this finding and to determine whether the establishment of care programmes will in time indeed lead to a more process-oriented view of professionals.

model_explanation: Based on the retrieved evidence, there is no previous description of cerebromediastinal tuberculosis in an immunocompetent child. However, the case presentation suggests a probable causative link between Say-Barber-Miller syndrome and tuberculosis. The syndrome's characteristic facial dysmorphism, microcephaly, mental retardation, and recurrent infections may be associated with an increased susceptibility to tuberculosis. While there is no direct evidence of a causal relationship, the coincidence of these conditions raises the possibility that Say-Barber-Miller syndrome may increase the risk of developing tuberculosis, including cerebromediastinal tuberculosis in children.
long_answer: [corrected] This observation is exceptional in many aspects: very early age of onset of extrapulmonary tuberculosis, no immune deficit, association with a rare congenital neurological syndrome. We discuss the possible link between this entity and the occurrence of tuberculosis.

model_explanation: The results from the reliability study suggest that ISAC 112 is a moderately reliable method for detecting specific IgE antibodies. The mean coefficient of variation (CV) was 9.4%, indicating variability between assays and batches. Intra- and inter-assay agreements were "very good" to most allergens, but moderate or poor agreements were observed in some cases. Inter-laboratory variations were also noted, with "good" agreements found in 22 out of 73 samples. Overall, the results indicate that while ISAC 112 is generally reliable, it should be used with caution and interpreted in the context of clinical results.
long_answer: The allergen microarray immunoassay, ISAC 112, is a repeatable and reproducible in vitro diagnostic tool for determination of sIgE beyond the own laboratory.

model_explanation: The retrieved evidence suggests that schizophrenia patients with exceptionally high pre-morbid intelligence may represent a clinically distinct subtype. High-IQ individuals showed lower scores on negative and disorganized symptoms, better global functioning, and insight compared to those with typical IQ. They also experienced less decline in IQ post-onset. This indicates that cognitive abilities may influence symptom presentation and prognosis in schizophrenia. However, further research is needed to confirm the existence of a distinct subtype and explore its implications for diagnosis, treatment, and patient outcomes. More study is required to fully understand this phenomenon.
long_answer: These findings provide evidence for the existence of a high-IQ variant of schizophrenia that is associated with markedly fewer negative symptoms than typical schizophrenia, and lends support to the idea of a psychosis spectrum or continuum over boundaried diagnostic categories.

model_explanation: Yes, based on the retrieved evidence, halofantrine appears to be ototoxic.
